Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

pat-a-cake noun

the clapping game

also patty-cake, pat a cake, clapping game, clap hands

classical

Cic. Att. 16.2.3 (Lewis & Short s.v. plaudō): manūs suās in plaudendō cōnsūmere
Ps. 46 [47], 2: plaudite manibus

manibus plaudere

clap one’s hands

No ancient clapping rhyme is known; plaudō is the classical verb for clapping the hands.

Examples

  • Omnēs gentēs, plaudite manibus; jūbilāte Deō in vōce exsultātiōnis

    Clap your hands, all you nations; shout to God with a voice of joyPs. 46 [47], 2

  • Manibus plaudāmus!

    Let’s clap our hands!composed

Other words

  • manūs complōdere — clap the hands together

    also used · classical · Quint. 11.3.123; Petr. 18.7 (Lewis & Short s.v. complōdō)

    Post-Augustan prose, of clapping for joy or grief (Lewis & Short).

See also game, song, cake.

SourcesLewis & Short: plaudo · Lewis & Short: complodo

The psalm from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-vulgata).

No ancient clapping rhyme is known; the call is ours, built on the classical verb.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
